definitions: To claim complete responsibility and praise for an achievement or action, often implying that one is solely responsible, even if others contributed.
To accept all the recognition and honor for a particular success or accomplishment.
examples: She was quick to take full credit for the successful project, even though her team did most of the work.
Don't let him take full credit for your ideas; make sure your contributions are recognized.
It's unfair when one person tries to take full credit for a group effort.
